name: inprocess-obi-axi4lite-axiluart-zipdma-f1f6-fuzz
notes: same CPU, same Wishbone DMA and same fixed RAM image as configs/scenarios/inprocess-obi-apb-ibex-timer-zipdma-f1f6.json; only the target changed, so the two runs differ in exactly the target protocol

the target is the pinned ZipCPU axiluart AXI4-Lite slave (C_AXI_ADDR_WIDTH=4, window 16 bytes) behind the generated axi4_lite_mmio_bridge: register map SETUP 0 (rw), FIFO_STATUS 4 (ro), RXREG 8 (rw), TXREG 12 (rw)
rx=1 and cts_n=0 are the pin constants the phase-one descriptor declared for this slave; the entry renders them from the generated model's own input rows (IP_FIXED_INPUTS)
target_window 0x40000000..0x4000000f and dma_window 0x40001000..0x4000100f do not overlap and both clear the 4 GiB bound

F5 is not declared here and the entry refuses it by name (unsupported-f5:target-irq-semantics:axi4-lite:...): the UART's four interrupt outputs are level sources that rise on serial RX activity or on FIFO occupancy, and none of them is raised by a write to a declared register.  The tx/txfifo sources are asserted at reset (TX FIFO empty), so wiring them would interrupt the CPU outside any F5 case instead of inside a declared trigger sequence.  This entry does not drive the serial RX pin over time, so the run covers F1-F4 and F6 and states the refusal instead of inventing an F5
F4 uses TXREG (offset 12): a write to it really pushes the TX FIFO, so the AXI4-Lite write has a device effect and not just a handshake
all three profiles declare 50 MHz except the ZipDMA's nominal 1 Hz simulation rate, so assume_single_clock states that one host tick drives all three models
fuzz mode: F1-F4 and F6 are offered; F5 stays refused by name because the AXI4-Lite UART declares no register-triggered interrupt
